channel.title: Acme: Light News
channel.description: Positive, lighthearted and unusual current news.

item.title: Native wildlife rebounds after rats and pigs leave a Samoan island
item.description: A year after community-led teams removed invasive rats and feral pigs from Nu'utele, native seedlings carpet parts of the forest, giant taro is growing again and vulnerable birds are nesting. Conservationists also found a land-crab species not previously recorded on the island.

item.title: Strangers rally around an 86-year-old's 39-year boat project
item.description: Dale began welding a 62-foot steel boat in his Texas yard in 1987, hoping to sail it to Alaska. Three visiting Britons shared his story and started a fundraiser; more than 1,500 donors quickly contributed over $41,000 to help finish the vessel, move it down a steep hill and launch it.

item.title: A simpler process recovers 98 percent of used acrylic glass
item.description: ETH Zurich researchers devised a solvent-free method that turns used acrylic glass back into pure building blocks at roughly half the heat older methods require. It recovered up to 98 percent of the material, even from dyed or impure samples, and can work with existing industrial equipment.

item.title: Ten-year-old dog returns after a month alone in Yellowstone
item.description: Luna, a Jack Russell terrier, survived more than a month among Yellowstone's bears, wolves and freezing nights after escaping a cabin. Volunteer Katie Boucher and one of Luna's owners finally found her in a live trap baited with scraps from a family shirt and pillowcase. She was underweight but alert and ready for home.

item.title: Texas barber returns $128,514 left atop an ATM
item.description: An anonymous Lewisville barber found a cash-stuffed bag and 19 checks on a bank ATM, then immediately called police. Investigators traced the $128,514 to Bank of America after a repair technician apparently forgot it. The bank recovered every dollar, and police plan to honor the finder privately at his request.

item.title: Students turn a staged cafeteria fight into a principal's birthday surprise
item.description: Georgia principal Bobby Davis raced toward what looked like a cafeteria brawl, only for the crowd to shout “Happy Birthday.” The organizer was De'Zayviun Watkins, a 17-year-old who credits Davis with helping him control his anger and discover poetry, music and a career goal. The prank became a heartfelt thank-you to a mentor.

item.title: A lightning survivor proposes to the woman who restarted his heart
item.description: Nick and Eva Broderick were struck by ground current during a Wisconsin hike, leaving Nick without a pulse. Eva performed CPR and revived him twice during the 50-minute wait for rescuers. After his recovery, he proposed; they married nearly a year later, and she received a lifesaving award.

item.title: Mozambique protects a mountain forest rich in butterflies
item.description: Mozambique has created a 23,000-acre community conservation area around Mount Mabu, a secluded rainforest known to harbor more than 200 butterfly species and exceptional endemism. Local communities will help manage the protected forest under a plan combining biodiversity protection with sustainable livelihoods.

item.title: Artists recreate a 700-year-old Met mural and uncover a hidden quirk
item.description: Chinese artists and conservators spent three years producing a life-size replica of the Metropolitan Museum's 50-foot Medicine Buddha mural. Their close study revealed that the central Buddha's head was mounted about two centimeters out of alignment, a detail the monumental work had concealed for centuries.

item.title: A village knits its own traffic police to slow drivers
item.description: Residents of Fillongley, England, installed life-size knitted police officers and speed cameras at a dangerous junction. The woolly patrol took four months to make, and villagers say drivers are already braking when they spot it.

item.title: Retired couple receives a surprise new heating and cooling system
item.description: Diane and Brian Johnsen of Beaverton, Oregon, were surprised with a new heating and cooling system worth about $16,000. The gift came through Lennox’s Feel the Love program, which has helped more than 3,100 families since 2009.

item.title: Eight rescued orangutans return to a protected Borneo forest
item.description: Conservationists released eight endangered orangutans into Indonesia’s protected Batu Nyambu forest after rescuing them from wildfires. The group includes three mothers with infants and two adolescent males; all had recovered from dehydration and malnutrition.

item.title: How Snoopy's flight made a Halloween classic
item.description: A look back at “It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown” explains how Snoopy's Red Baron fantasy helped turn animation into cinematic storytelling. It also reveals that Linus's iconic pumpkin patch scene was nearly left out and how a sound editor created Snoopy's unusual sob.

item.title: Family assembles 1,601 squirt guns for a record bid
item.description: A Mechanicsville, Virginia, family spent years gathering 1,601 squirt guns and has submitted the collection for Guinness recognition. The arsenal ranges from tiny novelty sprayers to enormous Super Soakers, all carefully counted and photographed.

item.title: Escaped pelicans return safely to the Pittsburgh Zoo
item.description: Two pelicans flew out of their Pittsburgh Zoo habitat, prompting a riverfront search by zoo staff and local rescue crews. Both birds were recovered unhurt and returned for checkups, ending the unexpected excursion safely.
